Generative Demos

Controllable generative models — GeoDiffuser (WACV 2025 Best Student Paper), GenHSI (WACV 2026), AppearancePointers (under review).

Across these three projects I build legible, designed structures inside the forward pass of pretrained diffusion models — so a user can control where content goes, what it looks like, and how it moves, without retraining the base model. For full write-ups: GeoDiffuser, AppearancePointers, GenHSI.

WACV 2025 · Best Student PaperGeoDiffuser

Geometry-based image editing on a frozen text-to-image diffusion model — training-free, invited talk at WACV 2025. User specifies a 3D rigid transformation (translate, rotate, scale) on an object; GeoDiffuser realizes it by rewriting the model's attention maps at inference time, preserving physically-consistent shadows and reflections.

WACV 2026Training-freeGenHSI

Training-free controllable generation of long human–scene interaction (HSI) videos. The user supplies three things — an image of a scene, an image of a character / avatar, and a text prompt describing a chain of interactions — and GenHSI synthesizes a long, 3D-aware video of the character performing those interactions inside the scene, with identity preservation and physically plausible affordances. No fine-tuning of the base video-diffusion model.

Three-stage pipeline inspired by movie animation: (1) Script writing — a VLM parses the high-level text prompt into atomic actions grounded in the scene's affordances; (2) Pre-visualization — a pretrained 2D inpainting diffusion model is used to generate plausible 2D human poses via view canonicalization, which are then lifted to 3D keyframes under contact + VLM reasoning; (3) Animation — the 3D keyframes condition a pretrained video-diffusion model to render the final long interaction video.

Project page IVL mirror arXiv

Authors: Zekun Li, Rui Zhou, Rahul Sajnani, Xiaoyan Cong, Daniel Ritchie, Srinath Sridhar.

Same instinct as GeoDiffuser — use a pretrained generative model as a compositional substrate without retraining — carried from 2D image editing to 3D-aware long-form video generation.

Under review · ICLR 2027AppearancePointers

Fine-grained multi-region controllable image generation on FLUX / MMDiT. Every region in the output can be independently specified by a different modality — text, reference image, or material texture — without region bleed, in a single denoising pass. Introduces per-region appearance-pointer tokens plus a position-ID resampling scheme that routes each conditioning signal to its designated spatial region.

Project page IVL mirror arXiv
Per-region control via text, reference image, or material texture — in a single denoising pass of a pretrained FLUX / MMDiT model.

Method overview

Region tokens attach appearance pointers that route conditioning to their spatial regions via position-ID resampling in the attention layers.

Qualitative results

Multi-region generations with mixed conditioning modalities per region.

Headline results: Beats DreamRenderer, MSDiffusion, InstanceDiffusion, and Seg2Any — gold on CLIP-I / DINO-I / MIoU for image-conditioned region generation, and gold on CLIP-I / DINO-I for text-conditioned. Also curated and released AP-37K, a 37K-sample multimodal dataset of text + reference-image + texture conditioning triplets.
